chapter: Leaving St. Louis: Toby show, Darrell Harris and Eli Rice
title: Stranded in Ludington; Eli Rice called
summary: The band never earned a quarter. Harris tried to steal the money and leave them stranded in Ludington, Michigan, so Willy Berel called Minneapolis bandleader Eli Rice.

bands.name: Darrell Harris and his Black Diamond Orchestra

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: How long, after you were with Darrell Harris' band, what do you do next?
Well, that's a good question. Because we got stranded.
In a place called Luddington, Michigan. So, some Willy (Barell.)

Yes. And his wife, May, and I think they were living out of Minneapolis. They knew some people in Minneapolis with some musical ideas so we all broke. And May is sick so he said well, I'm going to call Minneapolis. I know a band leader up there by the name of Eli Rice. Out of this Al Lewis (?) band and Darrell Harris' band -- Darrell Harris' band was the Black Diamond Orchestra.

Yeah, Darrell Harris' is the Black Diamond Orchestra. We never made a quarter. Not one quarter. So, we got stranded in Luddington so he called and we were staying with a white family there and a lady and her daughter. Tremendous people.
Things got kind of rough there. Musically rough. But, this cat wanted to steal the money. That's exactly what happened. He wanted to steal the money and split.

Yeah. Darrell Harris. Leave us stranded. Didn't leave a cent. Now, we're sitting there in the living room and eating these people's food and all that kind of thing. Giving us the go sign. We went there the first time and we looked so bad, we had our bags and everything and they refused us. I think it's a little resort town, right up the peninsula down on the lake ... so some fellow there They didn't want us recommended this young lady ... so anyhow we went down and we had a place to stay, which was important. And, we had a date. I think it may have been Luddington on the Lake ... beautiful spot. That's a spot you get off the nut to peek. All these other places have folded, this is the (...) off the nut. Also the spot where Darrell Harris would get off the nut. And leave us. But, the kiddies ... Somewhere during the course of the ideas ... trumpet player, a good buddy of mine, also a good buddy of Darrell Harris' told us what was happening because he (knew ?) ... to Fort Wayne. Now we got there, we are stranded. ... So, well, pride goes a long ways. I didn't send home for any money. In the first place I couldn't ... the idea within myself and, the second place, there was no money to be sent for. Do you know what I mean? So, Willy (Barell) calls Minneapolis. He scrapes some money together, calls Minneapolis and a fellow by the name of Eli Rice had a band. Tremendous name in that
part of the country. Tremendous person after I found out later. And this alto player by the name of George Johnson and he was there. So, he's a trumpet and alto saxophone player.
